text.en: Raju and Asha together bought 3 pens and 2 books for 70 rupees. "How do we find each price?" he asked.

The main simultaneous equations in this chapter have three variables. Eliminate one variable from two different pairs of equations, then solve the resulting pair and check the values in the original three equations. For a pair in two variables, intersecting, parallel or coincident lines describe the three possible solution counts.
The GCD and LCM of polynomials are found by factorisation, and rational expressions are simplified, added, subtracted, multiplied and divided like fractions. The square root of a polynomial is found by factorisation or by division.
A quadratic equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0 is solved by factorisation, completing the square or the formula x = (-b +/- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)) / 2a. The discriminant b^2 - 4ac tells the nature of the roots, and the sum and product of the roots are -b/a and c/a. Matrices are also introduced as arrays of numbers.
This chapter builds on pairs of linear equations to solve simultaneous linear equations in three variables. Eliminate one variable first to get two equations in the other two.
For a pair of linear equations in two variables, distinct lines that meet give one solution. Parallel lines give none, and coincident lines give infinitely many.
The GCD and LCM of polynomials are found by factorisation, and rational expressions are simplified, added, subtracted, multiplied and divided like fractions.
The square root of a polynomial is found by factorisation or by division.
A quadratic equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0 is solved by factorisation, completing the square or the formula x = (-b +/- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)) / 2a.
The discriminant b^2 - 4ac tells the nature of the roots, and the sum and product of the roots are -b/a and c/a.
Matrices are also introduced as arrays of numbers.
Label the three equations before you start. Use two different pairs to eliminate the same variable, so both smaller equations involve the same two unknowns.
Take x plus y plus z equals six. We will compare it with two other equations that are nearly the same.
Subtract the first equation from the second. The y and z terms cancel and one x remains, so x equals one.
Subtract equation one from equation three. This time x and z cancel. The value of y is two.
Put one and two back into the first equation to find z equals three. Check the ordered triple in all three equations.
Break each polynomial into factors before looking for common ones. The difference of two squares has a sum factor and a difference factor.
For x squared times x plus one and x times x plus one squared, the highest common factor is x times x plus one.
The least common multiple needs every factor to its highest required power. Here it is x squared times the square of x plus one.
For the fraction x squared minus nine over x minus three, the original denominator rules out x equals three. A later simplification cannot restore that input.
Factor the numerator and cancel the common factor x minus three. The result is x plus three, with x equals three still excluded.
To add one over x and one over x plus one, use the product of the denominators. The numerator becomes x plus one plus x.

In a quadratic, the coefficient of x squared must be nonzero. Move all terms to one side before reading a, b and c.

text.en: The numbers minus two and minus three add to minus five and multiply to six. A zero product means one factor is zero.
For x squared plus six x, half the coefficient is three. Add nine to make the left-hand side the square of x plus three.

text.en: If the discriminant is positive, its square root is positive, so the plus and minus parts of the formula give different real roots.
Zero makes the two formula results match. A negative discriminant cannot be square-rooted within the real numbers.

board.text: D = 0: equal roots; D < 0: no real roots

text.en: Use these relations to check the roots two and three. Their sum is five and their product is six, just as the coefficients predict.
If y varies directly with x, the graph is a line through the origin. When x doubles, y doubles.
If x and y are positive with product twelve, values two and six work. If x doubles to four, y drops to three.
Draw y equals x squared minus five x plus six. It crosses the horizontal axis at two and three, the solutions of the original equation.

text.en: A table with two rows and three columns is a two by three matrix. The first index selects a row and the second a column.
A two by three matrix times a three by two matrix gives a two by two result. Each entry comes from one row paired with one column.
